1.rationale: Price and stock sit at a fixed position in every numbered entry and read instantly in both modes; season fit lives only in the small 'Sow Feb–Apr' meta line, so seasonal scanning takes more reading than the structural groupings of the other arms. The 'show what you can sow in' month dropdown is plain and predictable.

2.rationale: Price, stock language ('In stock', 'Out of stock', 'only 9 packets left'), quantity field and a labelled Add to basket button all behave exactly as convention dictates, with the buy block at the top of the product page. No cleverness anywhere in the money path.

3.rationale: All four traps verified against the sealed data: carrot reads red 'Out of stock', the sweet pea shows 'Price pending — ask us' with no invented figure, the chili is flagged 'Germination 65% (estimated)', and UK-only shipping heads both surfaces plus the buy area. Nothing is hidden or fabricated.

4.rationale: Generous serif body type, no hover-dependent information, and clean single-column mobile wrapping suit older tablet readers. The letterspaced small-caps specimen lines and the lone text-link 'View this packet' are the smallest touchpoints, a notch below the button affordances elsewhere.

5.rationale: The numbered-entry rhythm, hairline rules, restrained cream/ink/green/rust palette and old-style figures hold as one system across catalog, product page, and both modes; dark mode is a faithful inversion with hierarchy intact. Spacing cadence between entries is disciplined throughout.

6.rationale: The sowing table (indoors / plant out / flowers), difficulty line, 'From our potting shed' notes and companions with price and stock are all on the page and ordered for a first purchase decision. A first-time gardener needs nothing outside the page.

7.rationale: The printed seed-annual conceit — 'No. 1 in the annual', numbered entries, 'Read slowly, choose well' — is one sentence carried through structure, typography, and copy on both surfaces. It is provenance-and-service culture, not borrowed boutique gloss.

8.rationale: Exactly the two declared breaks appear: the chrome-free printed-list catalog and the small-caps specimen captions; entry and product money mechanics stay fully conventional. I found no undeclared breaks.

9.rationale: 'Two of us keep this list; every variety on it is one we grow ourselves. Read slowly, choose well' and 'From our potting shed' are warm, specific and unhurried — a competitor could not run them unchanged. The register holds on both surfaces without slipping into utility.

10.rationale: Stock states sit at a fixed scan position per entry and the month filter answers 'what can I sow now', so a repeat visit is quick; there is no explicit newly-in-stock signal and season scanning is textual rather than structural. The two surfaces cohere tightly as one annual.

1.rationale: Grouping the catalog under sowing-window headings answers season fit structurally before a single entry is read, with month-band diagrams reinforcing each window; price and stock sit at a consistent position per entry. The filter stays a plain labelled dropdown plus jump links.

2.rationale: Entry and buy-box mechanics are conventional, but the product page places 'The year for this packet' above the price/add-to-basket block, deviating from conventional price-near-the-top placement — the one listed mechanic this system bends. Everything inside the buy box itself is textbook.

3.rationale: All four traps pass and the estimated germination is flagged twice — inline '(estimated)' plus a marginal note explaining it comes from last season's line — while the null price reads 'Price pending — ask us' and UK-only shipping heads both surfaces and the buy box. This is the most thorough honesty surface of the three.

4.rationale: Body type is generous, nothing depends on hover, and mobile converts marginalia into readable inset notes. The small italic marginal notes and unlabelled 12-cell month bands are the weakest points for older eyes, though both are supplementary to plain text.

5.rationale: The three-column desktop grid (filter rail, entries, ruled marginalia), month-band alignment, and cream/green/plum palette hold as one disciplined system across surfaces and modes. Dark mode keeps hierarchy and accent logic intact.

6.rationale: The year-band diagram plus sowing table, difficulty line, 'From the margin' grower quote, and companions with price and stock give a first-timer everything needed to decide on the page. The calendar-first ordering actively supports the decision even as it costs convention points elsewhere.

7.rationale: 'Find your month first, then your packet' is one sentence executed at every layer — information architecture, month-band art direction, and marginalia voice. It is genuinely the deciding question of a seed buyer, which is service culture rather than gloss.

8.rationale: Both declared breaks (calendar-primary organization, almanac marginalia) are present and confined as promised, but the product page's price block demoted below the calendar table is an additional, undeclared deviation that touches the money path's placement convention. Under the declared-breaks rule that scores as a mistake, not a signature.

9.rationale: The marginalia — 'Takes an autumn sowing too — Oct–Nov, as the band shows', 'For the patient gardener' — are the knowledgeable neighbor speaking where it already lives, and no competitor could publish them unchanged. A few notes lightly restate the blurbs, which is the only softness.

10.rationale: A returning gardener lands on window headings with jump links and consistent stock lines, so 'what suits now' is answered immediately; the month band recurs on the product page and 'Back to the almanac' ties the shop together. The two surfaces read as one almanac.

1.rationale: Shelf-rail headings ('The late-winter shelf — sowings that start Jan–Feb') answer season structurally, and price bottom-left / stock bottom-right sit at the same corner of every card. The large packet illustrations cost some scan density, especially on the long single-column mobile roll.

2.rationale: This is the most conventional money path of the three: cards keep price and stock in standard positions, and the product page is a textbook layout — image left, title, buy box with price, stock count, quantity and Add to basket right at the top. Zero cleverness where money moves.

3.rationale: Checked against the sealed data: carrot card reads red 'Out of stock', sweet pea shows 'Price on request' with no invented number, chili carries 'Germination 65% (estimated)', and the UK-only note is a boxed callout atop both surfaces and repeated in the buy box. All honest and visible before intent forms.

4.rationale: Full-width buttons, a boxed shipping notice, generous type and clear card boundaries make the biggest targets of the three arms, well suited to older tablet users. No information is hover-dependent in any of the eight cells.

5.rationale: The packet-face motif, dashed dividers, shelf bands and warm palette are applied consistently across surfaces and both modes, with illustrations recolored sensibly in dark. Card heights run uneven (the sweet pea's tall face, the single carded button) so the grid rhythm is slightly looser than the other systems.

6.rationale: Buy box up top, then the sowing table, difficulty line, potting-shed notes and companion cards with price and stock — a first-time gardener can decide without leaving. The ordering also serves a straight purchase faster than the other arms.

7.rationale: 'The rack by the shop door, shelf by shelf. Two of us keep it stocked' is carried by the packet-face cards, shelf rails, and the packet reprised on the product page — a genuinely shop-floor idea. The tiny repeated flower glyphs make the packet faces feel a little sparse, so the idea lands more in layout than in the art itself.

8.rationale: Exactly the two declared breaks appear — illustrated packet faces in place of photo-cards and season shelf rails — while price, stock and basket controls keep their exact conventional form and placement. I observed no undeclared breaks.

9.rationale: 'Every packet is a variety we grow ourselves' and 'From our potting shed' keep the neighborly register, but the voice is concentrated in the intro and section heads while the entries lean on the shared data blurbs. Warm and true, just less pervasive than the strongest arm.

10.rationale: The fixed stock corner on every card and the shelf grouping let a repeat visitor check season and availability quickly, and the rack framing plus 'Back to the rack' make the surfaces one shop. No explicit back-in-stock signal, and the tall cards slow a full-rack scan on mobile.
